output:
**What I found:** Don't build the plugin system now. The record calls this DROP: you'd be adding a way to plug in output formats when only one format exists and nobody has asked for a second.

**Why it matters:** A plugin system becomes a promise to outside users as soon as someone writes a plugin against it, so it's hard to take back. You'd also have to keep it working and tested through every future change. If you skip it, you lose very little: adding a second format later means changing one spot in the code.

**Do this first:**
1. Check that all JSON output goes through one function. If calls are scattered, pull them into one function. That's the only preparation worth doing now.

**What I did not check:**
- I didn't look at your code, since no repository was given. Whether JSON output is already in one place can be checked with `rg "json\.dumps|JSON\.stringify|json\.Marshal|serde_json" <src>`.
- No usage data or request tracker was available. I relied on your statement that nobody has asked for another format.

```
Dispatch:   DIRECT
Core route: M
Companions: None
Execution:  single-agent — one gate, no independent work packages
```

```
Subject:        Plugin system for CLI output formats
Mode:           Prospective
Necessity:      Fail
Necessity note: §1a generality without instantiation. A plugin interface needs several
                implementations or outside authors. There is one format (JSON), no request
                for a second, and no named outside plugin author.
                §8a optionality fails: no next format is named, so the option is speculative.
Outcome evidence: none
Decision:       DROP
Rationale:      The problem the plugin system solves (adding formats without changing the
                tool) does not exist today. A plugin API is also hard to reverse (§8b): once
                outsiders depend on it, it is a public contract that limits every later
                change to output. Adding a second format to code that has one formatter
                function is a local change, so waiting costs almost nothing.
Next action:    Keep JSON output behind one formatter function. Add no --format flag, no
                registry and no plugin loader.
Verification:   Not run (no codebase given). Run the rg command above to confirm one
                serialization point.
Minimal alt:    When a second format is requested, add a --format flag and a plain internal
                switch over built-in formatters. Consider plugins only when people outside
                the project need to ship formats without changing the tool.
Revisit when:   (a) someone concretely asks for a second output format → build the internal
                switch, or (b) an outside party needs to add formats without changing the
                tool → reconsider a plugin API.
```
